Biryar reads your own Amazon seller account: the sales Amazon has paid
out and the fees on them, your listings and their prices, and what is in
stock. Amazon lets a program do that only through an *application*, a
kind of visitor's pass that you register yourself, and only after you, as
the seller, have given that application permission.

This is the step most likely to lose someone, so this guide is written to
be read in order, with screenshots, and it says what goes wrong as well as
what to do.

## In short

| | What you do | How long |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Register as a developer with Amazon, for your own business only | A form, then Amazon reviews it. Allow a few days. |
| 2 | Create an application, with four permissions ticked | Five minutes |
| 3 | Authorise it against your own account, and paste four values into Biryar | Five minutes |

You end up with four values, all pasted once under **Settings,
Connections**:

| Value | What it is |
|---|---|
| Client ID | Your application's identifier, under its LWA credentials in Amazon's portal |
| Client secret | The secret that goes with it |
| Merchant token | Your seller id, shown when you authorise |
| Refresh token | A long text beginning `Atzr|`, which Amazon shows once when you authorise |

Biryar locks all four away on your computer the moment they are saved and
never shows them again: not on the screen, not in a log.

> Amazon renames and rearranges this part of Seller Central more often
> than it updates its instructions. Where this guide and the screen in
> front of you disagree, the screen is right. Please tell us at
> info@ciyalabs.com, so this page gets fixed.

## What Biryar asks permission for

Four permissions, which Amazon calls roles:

| What for | Amazon's name for the operation | Role it needs |
|---|---|---|
| Your paid-out sales and fees | `listTransactions`, Finances API | **Finance and Accounting** |
| Your listings, as a report | `GET_MERCHANT_LISTINGS_ALL_DATA`, Reports API | **Product Listing** |
| One listing's price, minimum and maximum | `getListingsItem`, Listings Items API | **Product Listing** |
| Who else sells it, and the Featured Offer | `getItemOffers`, Product Pricing API | **Pricing** |
| What is in FBA stock | `getInventorySummaries`, FBA Inventory API | **Amazon Fulfillment** |
| **Sending a price** (Pro, switched on) | `patchListingsItem`, Listings Items API | **Product Listing** |

None of them is a restricted role. Nothing here gives access to buyers'
names or addresses, so you are not applying for personal data and not
waiting on a separate approval for it. [[3]](#sources)

Biryar changes exactly one thing on Amazon, and only if you let it: the
price of a listing. That happens only on Pro, only after you switch
sending on under Settings, only for listings you turned on, and never
outside the minimum and maximum you set in Seller Central. Biryar cannot
edit a listing's text, touch an order or send a message. The roles for
those are not on the list.

If a later version needs another role, it will say so and ask again. It
cannot quietly widen what it already has: the roles are fixed on the
application, and adding one requires you to authorise again.

## Step 1: register as a developer

Amazon has to know who is behind an application before it lets you create
one.

Go to <https://solutionproviderportal.amazon.com> and sign in. It is a
separate sign-in, though it is the same Amazon account, and if you have
more than one selling account it asks which to use first.

Older instructions, including Amazon's own, send you to **Apps and
Services, Develop Apps** in Seller Central. [[2]](#sources) On a current
account that menu entry is gone. This was checked against a live German
seller account in November 2026: the section is now called **Programs and
apps**, it has no Develop Apps in it, and the old address shows this
before sending you on:

![Seller Central announcing that Developer Central now forwards to the
Solution Provider Portal](/docs/setup/img/developer-console-redirect.jpg)

Once you are in, the portal's front page is the whole working area: the
status of your developer profile at the top, and your applications below
it.

![The Solution Provider Portal front page, with the developer profile
reviewed and one application in Draft](/docs/setup/img/solution-provider-portal-apps.jpg)

If you have never registered, complete the developer profile here first.
[[2]](#sources) The form asks for contact details, what data you want and
why, and how you keep it safe, and ends with a box to accept Amazon's
agreements.

**The one answer that matters** is in the **Data Access** section. Choose
the option for a business that sells on Amazon and only wants to manage
its own business. Amazon words it as *"My organization sells on Amazon,
and I only want to integrate to manage my own business only."*
[[2]](#sources) Choosing an option meant for software companies puts you
on a much longer review for no benefit.

Then wait. Amazon reviews the request and writes to the main email
address on the account. **If Amazon asks you for more information, answer
within five days**, or the request is closed and you start again.
[[2]](#sources)

This is the one step with a person at the other end. Nothing in Biryar
can shorten it.

## Step 2: create the application

In the portal, choose **Add new app client**. The whole form is four
questions:

![The app registration form: name, API type, business entities and
roles](/docs/setup/img/app-roles.jpg)

- **App name**: anything. It is shown to you, not to buyers.
- **API Type**: SP API.
- **Business entities**: Sellers.
- **Roles**: **Finance and Accounting**, **Product Listing**, **Pricing**
  and **Amazon Fulfillment**, the four from the table above.
  [[3]](#sources)

> Tick these four and nothing more. Every extra role is something a
> leaked key could reach. Product Listing is needed even if you never
> switch repricing on: it is the role that reads your listings.

Answer **no** to the question about giving another developer's
application access to personal data.

Leave the application in **Draft**. There is no reason to publish an
application that only you use [[1]](#sources), and publishing is a review
you do not need.

## Step 3: authorise it, and bring the values to Biryar

In the portal, open the application's **Action** menu. It has one entry:

![The app row's action menu, offering only Authorize](/docs/setup/img/app-actions-authorize.jpg)

Choose **Authorize**. Amazon gives your application permission for your
own account and shows you a **refresh token**, a long text beginning
`Atzr|`. It is shown once, so copy it straight away.

> Amazon allows ten of these per application, and there is no way to get
> more. [[1]](#sources) Every time you authorise again to get a fresh
> token, one is used. This dialog shows how many are left:

![The portal's authorisations dialog: ten self-authorisations, and
OAuthorizations "No authorization allowed"](/docs/setup/img/authorizations-remaining.jpg)

Then, in Biryar, open **Settings, Connections**. Under the Amazon card,
open **Connect with a refresh token** and enter the four values:

- **Merchant token** and **Refresh token**, from the step you just did.
- **Client ID** and **Client secret**, from the application's LWA
  credentials in the portal.

Press **Save**. Biryar checks the values with Amazon straight away and
refuses to store a set that does not work, so you find out now and not
later.

All four are needed, even though it is the token you were given. A refresh
token does not open anything by itself. Before every read Biryar swaps it
with Amazon for a pass that lasts one hour, and Amazon checks that swap
against the application's Client ID and secret.

After that, Biryar starts fetching your paid-out sales by itself. The
first fetch reaches back in time; later ones keep it up to date.

## When it goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_client` | The Client ID or Client secret does not belong to the application you authorised. | Enter both again, under **Change the application**, from the application's LWA credentials. |
| `MD9100` | You were sent to Amazon's consent page. An application that only you use has no such page. | Use **Connect with a refresh token**, as in step 3. |
| `403` from one of the reads | The application does not have that read's role. | Add the missing role from the table above to the application, and authorise again. [[3]](#sources) |
| `SPSA2043` | A vendor account whose group lacks the role needed to reach the authorise page. | Your vendor manager has to add the `SPDS-VC-MYA` role. [[1]](#sources) |
| Biryar says the authorisation needs renewing | The refresh token was withdrawn: after a password change, or because the authorisation was removed in the portal. | Authorise again and paste the new token. Biryar has stopped trying meanwhile. |
| The portal shows fewer authorisations than you expected | Each one uses one of ten, including the ones spent finding your way around. | Nothing. Use the remaining ones with care. |

`MD9100` looks like this in Seller Central:

![Seller Central answering MD9100, "this app does not have the right
application details"](/docs/setup/img/consent-md9100.jpg)

## Taking the permission back

You can withdraw the authorisation in Amazon's portal at any time. The
next time Biryar tries to read, it marks the connection as needing to be
authorised again and stops. Nothing in Biryar can prevent you from doing
this, which is how it should be for a program that holds a key to your
finances.

## Good to know

- **Which Amazon you sell on is worked out, not set.** A refresh token
  works in one region only, and Biryar picks the right one from your
  marketplace. Europe and North America are covered today.
- **About the screenshots.** They are from a real German seller account,
  taken in November 2026, with account names blurred. Amazon rearranges
  this area often, so treat them as what the screens looked like then.
